summary: A fast food worker supports a raise as a matter of fairness and resents being treated as unskilled.
realLife: A fast food worker supporting a family on a low hourly wage speaks plainly, in the budget of the week: rent takes most of the paycheck, food help sets the shopping day, and a sick child or a missed check is an emergency. She backs a higher wage on fairness grounds, resents the idea that her work is unskilled, and is bothered when new hires start near veterans' pay. She does not weigh job losses or small business costs, and names no party.
sources: https://www.mprnews.org/story/2020/03/05/what-its-like-to-support-a-family-on-1250-an-hour (public radio profile of a parent working fast food)
gates: the speaker works for an hourly wage near the minimum
